title: Pare Irrigation Farmer's Lunch
localName: Chakula cha Mkulima wa Mifereji — Wapare
community: Pare people of the Pare Mountains — the mountain farmer's midday meal
author: Mama Salima
desc: Pare Farmer's Lunch — the midday meal of the Pare mountain irrigation farmers. Yam stew with beans, greens, and pumpkin — a complete, nutritious, entirely plant-based meal that fuels the physical work of mountain terrace farming.
longDesc: The Pare people developed sophisticated irrigation systems (mifereji) on their mountain slopes long before European contact — channelling mountain water through carved channels to terraced fields. The farmers who maintained these systems needed a complete, nourishing midday meal. This simple yam, bean, and vegetable stew is that meal.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden. Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Add yam and pumpkin. Add water. Cover and cook 15 minutes.
Add cooked beans. Cook 8 more minutes.
Add greens on top. Cover 3 minutes.
chefTips: Add greens last — they wilt in 3 minutes and lose colour if overcooked.
cookingScience: See TZA252 for mountain vegetable stew science.
sustainabilityTips: The Pare mifereji irrigation system is one of Africa's oldest sustainable water management traditions.
culturalNote: The Pare mountain farmer's lunch is the food of one of Tanzania's most innovative agricultural traditions — the people who carved water channels into mountain rock to irrigate their terraced fields. The meal is as practical and ingenious as the irrigation system itself.
